preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= R <= 10**3 for R, _, _ in test_cases) and all(2 <= C <= 10**3 for _, C, _ in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, R and C are between 2 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= X <= min(R, C) for R, C, X in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, X is between 2 and the minimum of R and C inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(A) == R and len(row) == C for A, _, _, R, C in test_cases) and all(len(B) == R and len(row) == C for _, B, _, R, C in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, matrices A and B have R rows and C columns.

preconditions.expression: all(all(abs(A[i][j]) <= 10**9 for j in range(C)) for i in range(R)) and all(all(abs(B[i][j]) <= 10**9 for j in range(C)) for i in range(R))
preconditions.description: For each test case, all elements in A and B are between -10^9 and 10^9 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(output == 'Yes' or output == 'No' for output in outputs)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'Yes' or 'No'.

postconditions.expression: all((output == 'Yes') == (is_possible(A, B, R, C, X) for A, B, R, C, X, output in zip(test_cases_A, test_cases_B, test_cases_R, test_cases_C, test_cases_X, outputs)))
postconditions.description: The output 'Yes' is correct if and only if it is possible to transform matrix A into matrix B using the allowed operations. The output 'No' is correct otherwise.
